prompt: Create one flat stained-glass puzzle DESIGN SHEET, portrait 3:4. Reference images: first lighthouse and second fox are style references for elegant flowing leaded-panel composition, third old lighthouse is subject reference only. Redraw a striped lighthouse on rocks casting two broad beams over the sea at dusk. Center a tall ROUND ARCH panel almost touching canvas edges, closed black outer rim on pure white exterior. Aim 100-115 individually closed panes (allowed 88-128). Elegant hand-crafted glass geometry but entirely FLAT SOLID fills, NO texture, NO gradients, NO shadows or highlights. Exactly FOUR glass colours: vermilion #CC4B32 and golden amber #F2BA32 exclusively for the lighthouse subject; deep ocean blue #185577 and turquoise #259CA5 exclusively for ALL background including rocks, sea, sky and beams. Lighthouse stripes alternate vermilion and amber across the whole tower; windows use only these warm colours. Background beams are turquoise outlined wedges amid blue dusk, not yellow. Sky has flowing broad arcs; waves and coastal rocks give natural organic divisions. Alternate the two cool colours between neighbouring background pieces wherever possible. About 18-24 subject panes, remaining 75-90 background panes; clean readable architecture with a lantern room, conical roof, broad alternating tower bands and base. Uniform pure black smooth lead approximately 1 percent canvas width. Every line closes a pane, no loose ends, no X crossings, no four-way junctions: offset every meeting to separated T junctions at least 3 percent panel width apart. No tiny panes, no slivers, no close parallel lines, no arbitrary grid or border frame. No lettering or signature. Improve on the references by eliminating their shading, colour-pair mixing and X crossings. This is a traceable flat design, not final textured glass.
